page.layout: One page of text: a Latin verse poem set in a single column, with the catchword "Num" at the lower right below the last line. No margin notes.

main_text.p: Imbelles animas, ignauáq; pectora, Francúm Pudenda Carcinomata, Vos superis perdat iaculatus ab arcibus ignes Deus rubente dextera. Hoc vobis licuisse nefas? extinguere tantum Atro veneno Principem? Thessalicis ergo infidiis, atque artibus omnis Sanguis peribit regius? Gallica sic visum est aconitis sceptra parare Seu poculis Canidiæ? Tam vos regnandi rapuit vesana libido, & Caeci furoris impetus, Legibus ut spretis, nulla virtute, venenis, Periuriis, & cædibus, Legitimis tandem pulsis hæredibus, eheu! Gallos regatis, Aduenæ? Ah, Galli, quæ vos cæpit dementia? tantus Vos usq; vexabit furor? Illis ut regni tristes prodatis habenas, Artes malæ quos prouehunt. Scilicet his meritum grati referetis honorem, Laudisq; avitæ præmia? Scilicet auxerunt vestros virtute triumphos, Auxêre vestra commoda? Ecce Periclæo paces stratagemate turbant, Belloq; mutant ocia? Civiles ecce accendunt ad prælia dextras, Martémque inexpiabilem?

page.notes: Show-through from the facing page appears faintly on the right edge; ignored. "tantus" at the end of the line "Ah, Galli" is followed by a small ornament, not transcribed. A printed sign after "Aduenæ?" is shown as printed in the line; it reads as an ornament and is not transcribed. "pectora" in the first line is doubtful: the letters are blurred, read as "pectora" with [?] suggested. "infidiis" is doubtful: read as printed "infidiis" from a worn form.
